top_stories.title: OpenAI releases 722 math manuscripts from internal model
points: An internal, unreleased OpenAI model produced 722 manuscripts (grouped into 372 result families) tackling roughly 4,000 open problems in pure mathematics, theoretical computer science, and mathematical physics.
Boldest claim is a proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, a weaker cousin of the famous $1M Riemann Hypothesis about how prime numbers are distributed.
Most results took an average of just 3 hours of ChatGPT Pro compute (extended reasoning mode) per result, far less than last month's Navier-Stokes proof which needed 10,000 AI agents.
Many papers include Lean formalizations (software that mechanically verifies every logical step of a proof), though not all results have this, so some unformalized claims could still contain errors.

Reaction is split: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge called it 'the most significant moment in mathematical history,' while other mathematicians are angry OpenAI broke its promise to space out releases, and 28 mathematicians signed a September open letter opposing AI labs' use of unpublished research without credit.
The real bottleneck now is verification and absorption — how fast human mathematicians can check and build on the work — rather than how many results can be generated.

unique_angles.point: 162 of the papers include formal Lean proofs specifically.
Ten detailed reasoning summaries were published covering topics like π and spin glasses (physical systems of randomly oriented magnetic particles).
The release also included revision protocols and compute usage estimates in the GitHub repository.
OpenAI has specifically been accused of using unpublished mathematician research without consent or credit.

top_stories.title: Mistral launches 'Le Chonk' (Large 4), a 1-trillion-parameter open model
points: Mistral's Large 4, nicknamed 'Le Chonk,' is a 1-trillion-parameter (1,000 billion numerical values) open multimodal model positioned as Europe's answer to US and Chinese AI labs.
It claims to lead every non-Chinese open-weight system, reaching frontier-class status alongside GPT-6 Luna and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and supports 160+ languages.
Coding benchmark score of 62% beats Reflection's Beam (44%) but trails China's Kimi K3 (68%).
Claims top-5 global ranking in cybersecurity, scoring 82% on a bug-finding test that Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra mostly refused to attempt.
Scored nearly 3x higher than GPT-6 Astra on Harvey's legal benchmark per external testers (Vals), beating every Chinese open model tested.
Open-source weights are set to go public October 27, after a three-week preview for cyber experts.

top_stories.title: Anthropic's Claude integrates directly into Google Workspace
points: Anthropic launched a Claude sidebar/extension for Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides, letting Claude read and directly edit open files without copy-pasting between tabs.
Available now in public beta on all paid Claude plans.
Users can install it via Extensions → Claude inside any file, or start from a file link pasted into the Claude app.
Claude can edit directly or request approval before making changes.

top_stories.title: Hark Pro: proactive AI personal assistant from Figure AI founder
points: Brett Adcock (Figure AI founder) launched Hark Pro, a proactive personal AI assistant that remembers preferences, researches, shops, books events, and handles tasks like expense submission and subscription cancellation.
Demo: asked for two movie tickets, Hark picks seats, adds the show to the calendar, and offers to reserve parking without step-by-step direction.
Runs on Handoff, Hark's proprietary cloud system capable of operating up to 36 browsers simultaneously, showing clicks in chat for transparency.
Offers free and paid tiers; dedicated hardware devices are planned for 2027 via an AT&T partnership, competing with assistants like Muse, Grok Bot, Instinct, and Dots.

Sesame launched Personal Agents — assistants with their own dedicated computer that interact via text and speech, with AI glasses support arriving in 2027.
OpenAI is testing a Meetings plugin for ChatGPT's Mac app that turns meetings into personalized notes and next steps based on past work.
